failureMessage: the vendor set ships a pack only when declared, so a cross-pack import crashes every consumer that vendors one pack without the other
fix: declare the dependency (requires) and pass configuration, move the shared helper into engine/checks/helpers, or accept the import with a reason in .claudinite-settings.json

forbidReferences.reason: a pack imports only its own files, the engine surface, and the tasks pack's published public/ — abilities otherwise cross pack boundaries through declaration and configuration, never imports; a pack's updates/ is carved out because no vendor set carries it, so an import there cannot crash a consumer (#1317)

failureMessage: the directory name is the public id every member declares, so another casing costs a fleet-wide rename

forbidTrackedPathsMatching.what: a pack directory that is not kebab-case: {path}
forbidTrackedPathsMatching.fix: rename the directory to lowercase kebab-case before anyone declares it

failureMessage: a quoted count of checks or rules is stale at the next change; packs/README.md says how to count them

matchLines.fix: say how to count them instead of quoting the number

failureMessage: .claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/ exists only in the canon home, so the name dangles everywhere else the prose mounts

matchLines.what: names a home-only local pack path: {match}
matchLines.fix: point at the canon pack that owns the artifact, or describe it without its home path

failureMessage: the pack and engine lanes deliver on separate cadences, so a named import of an export the member's engine lacks is a link-time SyntaxError faulting the whole pack

checkSetValues.what: a pack imports the engine export {value} by name in the change that adds it
checkSetValues.fix: import the engine module as a namespace and guard the call with a typeof capability check

failureMessage: the tasks pack's roles are folders and the graph between them is one-directional — a stage reaching sideways or upwards is how the flat tree it replaced became unreadable
fix: move the shared thing down into contract/ or items/, or reach the other stage through the queue rather than through an import

forbidReferences.reason: what a task DECLARES is what every stage agrees on, so the contract names no stage and no port — a contract that read the world would make the thing being agreed on depend on who was asking, which is why the automerge verdict's git-reading command sits in src/session/ and the policy engine here decides

the work item as data, and the reads that fetch it: items names no stage, but the queue listing IS a GitHub read and a lease IS a clock read, so it reaches those through the ports like everything else
the ports are the only modules that reach outside, so they carry no stage's policy — a port that imported a stage would put a decision behind the seam a simulator replaces
collection reads the world through the ports and describes it in the contract's terms; it decides nothing, so it names no stage
the schedule asks whether a task's window has opened and files the item — what happens to that item afterwards is another stage's, reached through the queue and never through an import
the executor runs an item and hands its output to the delivery lane; it never reaches back into scheduling or into what a session does with the item it was handed
a session converges the item it was handed and lands its output; it is downstream of the executor and imports nothing from it
the landing lane is the bottom stage — it turns an output into a pull request and knows nothing about who produced it
repair reads the wreckage and files a report; it re-derives state rather than importing the stage that left it
adoption writes a member's workflows from the declarations and touches no running stage

`queue/` is frozen workflow ABI that re-exports the mechanism, so a module under src/ importing it would close a cycle through a path that exists only for outside callers; `public/` is different — its definition files (the vocabulary, the grammar, the GitHub client) are what src/ builds on

failureMessage: everything outside the run — GitHub, the Actions environment, subprocesses, the clock — is reached through packs/claudinite-tasks/src/world/, so a run can be driven at a chosen instant against a fake world
fix: call the port: makeGh and the named operation from src/world/github.mjs, actionsEnv/actionRepoContext from src/world/actions.mjs, runGit/startProcess from src/world/processes.mjs, now/nowMs/nowIso from src/world/clock.mjs

matchLines.what: calls fetch outside the world ports: "{match}"
matchLines.fix: reach GitHub through a named operation in src/world/github.mjs

matchLines.what: reads the environment outside the world ports: "{match}"
matchLines.fix: take the bag from actionsEnv(), or the named fact from src/world/actions.mjs

matchLines.what: starts a subprocess outside the world ports: "{match}"
matchLines.fix: call runGit or startProcess from src/world/processes.mjs

matchLines.what: reads the clock outside the world ports: "{match}"
matchLines.fix: call now() from src/world/clock.mjs — parsing a timestamp string is not a clock read and stays where it is

matchLines.what: reads the clock outside the world ports: "{match}"
